text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT 1755554321 - Routing anomalies from eu-west1 -> us-central. 3xx steering surge detected, latency spike > 400ms for 90s. Auto-fallback triggered for some routes. https://internal.ops/redwood/incidents/1755554321

maria.chen: seeing lots of 503s in customer-facing gateway logs. errors spike at 12:14 UTC.

sam.taylor: I'm onpager. digging into the steering telemetry now. can someone post the exact error pattern?

kevin.cho: top-line: we saw cross-region requests that should be pinned to eu-west1 getting routed to us-central during a policy evaluation window. TTLs are short but there was a simultaneous policy rollout 12:12-12:15.

alvaro: confirmed from traces: request header x-region-pref=eu-west1 but route decision returned us-central. looks like a policy evaluation race where the new rule returned a null and fell back to default region.

sam.taylor: ok that matches. customer impact: some customers in EU reporting latency >300ms and 5% error increase. severity?

maria.chen: support queue: 18 tickets flagged as "errors after deploy". SLO alert triggered. I'd mark P1 for now.

oncall-t1: oncall here. taking lead for mitigation. priority: stop bleed to wrong region and restore pinned routing for eu-west1.

kevin.cho: immediate mitigation option: roll back new steering policy or pin affected routes explicitly to eu-west1 for the duration. rollback is safest.

sam.taylor: what's deploy id for that policy?

kevin.cho: policy rollout id: pr-4827-eval. It was promoted at 12:11:37 UTC.

devops-bot: deploy-pr-4827-eval started -> promoting routing-policy v2.3.4 at 12:11:37 UTC (ci/team-routing).

alvaro: I can apply a quick pin override script to the route table to force eu-west1. It should be low-risk. Should we do rollback instead?

sre-rotation: quick check: how many instances in eu-west1 available? autoscaler shows spare capacity 10% only. If we pin more traffic there might hit capacity & cause throttles.

sam.taylor: good point. we should prefer rollback of the policy since it caused the mis-eval. rollback will restore previous deterministic behavior and avoid extra tail load.

oncall-t1: agreed. kevin, can you coordinate rollback? Maria, can you start customer comms & update status page?

kevin.cho: starting rollback now. running command: 
```
# roll back routing policy promotion
rbctl rollback --namespace=global-routing --policy=pr-4827-eval --to=stable-v2.3.3 --reason="mis-eval causing cross-region misroutes"
```

kevin.cho: running...

devops-bot: rollback job started (job id rb-1755554321-1). ETA ~ 35s.

maria.chen: posting incident note to status page: "Degraded routing for EU traffic causing higher latency and errors. Engineers rolling back recent routing policy. No data plane compromise suspected."

sam.taylor: live metrics - streaming: 
- error rate baseline 0.8% -> saw 5.2% at peak
- p95 latency baseline 120ms -> 380ms for eu users

alvaro: grep from trace sampler: 
```
TraceID: 0a1b2c - header region=eu-west1 -> decision=us-central (policy=null)
TraceID: 0a1b2d - header region=eu-west1 -> decision=eu-west1
```

kevin.cho: rollback complete. verifying routing table and control-plane cache flush. command: 
```
rbctl status --job=rb-1755554321-1
# then
routingctl flush-cache --scope=global --pattern="eu-*"
```

devops-bot: rollback job rb-1755554321-1 completed.

kevin.cho: cache flush in progress.

oncall-t1: monitoring for normalization. Sam, Maria keep me posted on customer-facing metrics.

sam.taylor: metrics updating: error rate dropping to 1.1% now, p95 latency 150ms and trending down.

maria.chen: support: updated customers and flagged follow-up Qs. added temporary note in messages: "We rolled back a routing policy that caused some EU traffic to be steered to US region; restoration in progress."

alvaro: double-checking policy evaluation logs: root cause appears to be a nil-return in evaluation when input included a legacy header format. The new policy expected header x-region and fell back to default. Edge cases for old clients didn't match new predicate.

kevin.cho: good catch. So root cause = policy predicate regression + rollout overlap. Postmortem action: add canary tests that include legacy header formats.

sre-rotation: note on capacity: after rollback we saw brief elevated load in eu-west1 but within headroom. no scaling failures.

sam.taylor: timeline update for incident timeline:
- 12:11:37 UTC policy pr-4827 promoted
- 12:13:15 UTC incident-bot anomaly triggered
- 12:14:00 UTC errors in support queue spike observed
- 12:15:10 UTC oncall paged and triage started
- 12:18:55 UTC rollback initiated
- 12:19:40 UTC rollback completed and cache flush started
- 12:23:05 UTC metrics start to normalize

maria.chen: impact estimate: 4.2% of EU requests affected, increased p95 for 15m window, ~20 customers observed elevated errors.

oncall-t1: escalation closed. assigning postmortem to alvaro + kevin. Please run blameless postmortem and schedule 1h retrospective.

alvaro: will produce postmortem draft. initial action items:
- add legacy-header test to policy canary suite
- gate rollouts with evals that include at least 2 traffic patterns
- add automatic rollback trigger when region steer mismatch >1%

kevin.cho: also add a runbook note: pinning vs rollback decision tree for oncall.

maria.chen: I'll work on customer communications follow-up and a consolidated incident update.

sre-rotation: tagging for follow-up: platform/steering, infra/autoscaler, devex/policy-rules.

sam.taylor: typing up the incident summary to paste into the ticket. good work team.

incident-bot: Incident 1755554321 resolved. Severity: P1 -> downgraded to P2 for follow-up. Postmortem owners: alvaro, kevin.

maria.chen: adding meeting invite for 2026-03-17 09:00 UTC for the postmortem review.

kevin.cho: extra note: checked DNS and no signs of TTL misbehavior; this was control-plane policy mis-eval not DNS.

alvaro: will include test snippets and logs in the postmortem. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
